Fact.Name: Had self-employment / gig / freelance income
Fact.Description: Interview gate: whether the filer (or spouse) had self-employment, gig, or freelance income that belongs on Schedule C. Gap evidence Pub 6048 excluded this from upstream Direct File: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p6048.pdf

Fact.Name: Wants qualified business income deduction (no longer asked)
Fact.Description: Kept so saved returns still load. The 26 U.S.C. 199A(a) deduction is not elective (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A), and Form 8995 (form8995.xml, #87) now computes it, so this answer is not used anywhere.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C QBI deduction case Form 8995 here can't compute
Fact.Description: #87: Schedule C qualified business income is computed on Form 8995 (form8995.xml). This is true when any Form 8995 stop applies: a prior-year loss carryforward, a cooperative patron, active and non-active businesses together, or taxable income before the deduction above the threshold (Form 8995-A). Each part is its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue fact in /flowIsKnockedOut and is complete false without Schedule C income (#186). Used for the Schedule C knockout screen.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses owned by the secondary filer
Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Sum of /scheduleCBusinesses/*/netProfitOrLoss for the businesses the secondary filer owns: the line 3 of that spouse's own Schedule SE. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE." $0 on a return that isn't a joint return (only a joint return reports a spouse's business) or when the filer answered no to self-employment income; incomplete while businesses are still being entered, like /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Every business not owned by the secondary filer is the primary filer's (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/filer defaults to the primary filer), so this is /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus /scheduleCSecondaryFilerNetProfitOrLoss, and the two always add up to Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Knockout: spouse-owned Schedule C business
Fact.Description: Schedule SE is figured per filer (scheduleSE /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentTax, with that spouse's own OASDI base under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)) and Schedule 2 line 4, Schedule 1 line 15 and Form 8959 line 13 combine both. A secondary filer's business still stops the return until the rest of that spouse's path is per spouse: EITC and CDCC earned income with self-employment (Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 are per spouse), and the printed return has no Schedule SE form yet (one per spouse once it does).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C cases the EITC, CDCC or ACTC earned income can't yet figure
Fact.Description: #117. The EITC (eitc /eitcEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay), the CDCC (income /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeForCdccBase) and the ACTC (income /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay) add /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome. Still stopped: - A Schedule C net loss. Both sources say a loss reduces earned income: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, line 1e and line 4b ("Combine lines 1e, 2c, 3, and 4a"), and the 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5 ("You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment"). /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome is floored at $0, so a loss stops the return when the EITC could apply (AGI below the EITC completed phaseout, eitc /belowEitcAgiLimit, or eitc /eitcQualified), the CDCC applies or the CTC applies. A loss can lower earned income below the EITC limit even when wages alone are above it, so the EITC test is on AGI, which already includes the loss. - A joint return with any Schedule C result and the CDCC: Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 need each spouse's Schedule SE line 3 and Schedule 1 line 15 share ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately"), and Schedule SE is not yet figured per spouse. Stopped elsewhere: a spouse-owned business (/flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness), statutory employees (formW2s /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee), and farm income, church employee income, the optional methods, ministry or Forms 4361 and 4029, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages (scheduleSE /flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). Complete and false when there is no Schedule C or the Schedule C result is a profit on a return that isn't a joint return claiming the CDCC.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales (derived)
Fact.Description: Gross receipts defaulting incomplete writable to zero for sums.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (MVP)
Fact.Description: MVP expense bucket (sum of deductible trade/business expenses). Authority: 26 U.S.C. § 162 (ordinary and necessary expenses paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162 Kept for a return that already stored one total. The interview now asks the Schedule C lines. Once any line-item answer is complete, this total is ignored.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (derived)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 28. On a return that only stored one expense total, that total. On the line-item path, the sum of the supported lines, and only when no out-of-scope form applies. Otherwise incomplete: an unanswered expense is not treated as zero. 26 U.S.C. 162(a).

Fact.Name: Net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31. Single-total path: gross receipts minus that total. Line-item path: line 7 minus line 28, and only when line 7 and line 28 are complete and no out-of-scope form applies. A loss that needs Form 6198 or Form 8582 is still computed and is stopped by /flowKnockoutScheduleCOutOfScope, because the stop reads this result and this result must not read the stop. 26 U.S.C. 61, 162, 465, 469.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business complete
Fact.Description: Single-total path: name, gross receipts, the expense total, and material participation. Line-item path: name, material participation, Part I amounts, and every stop question. A form stop completes the business without expense amounts. Otherwise the expense lines, line 7, and line 28 must be complete, and a loss needs the at-risk answer.

Fact.Name: Filer materially participates in this business
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B): "The term 'active qualified trade or business' means ... any qualified trade or business of the taxpayer in which the taxpayer materially participates (within the meaning of section 469(h))." 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): material participation means involvement in the operations of the activity "on a basis which is (A) regular, (B) continuous, and (C) substantial." Used for Form 8995 line 16 (minimum deduction).

Schedule C businesses with material participation

Fact.Name: Third other expense description
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part V description. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 17, Line 48: list the type of each expense separately.

Fact.Name: Third other expense amount
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part V amount. 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 17, Line 48.

Fact.Name: Has a second other expense
Fact.Description: Yes asks for a second Part V line. No leaves lines 2 and 3 of Part V blank.

Fact.Name: Has a third other expense
Fact.Description: Yes asks for a third Part V line.

Fact.Name: Has a fourth other expense
Fact.Description: The form has nine Part V lines. This tool supports three. A fourth stops the return. 2026 draft Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sc--dft.pdf), Part V.

Fact.Name: More than three Part V lines
Fact.Description: True only when the filer has a third other expense and still has another. False as soon as either 'another' answer is no.

Fact.Name: Part V line 2 amount included in the total
Fact.Description: Zero when that Part V line is not used.

Fact.Name: Part V line 3 amount included in the total
Fact.Description: Zero when the filer has no second Part V line, and zero when they have a second line but no third. Answering no to the first "another" question does not require the third-line question.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 27b and line 48
Fact.Description: Total other expenses. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 17: enter the total on lines 48 and 27b. Zero when other expenses were not chosen. Incomplete when amortization begins this year or a fourth line is needed.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 28
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sc--dft.pdf), line 28: total expenses before expenses for business use of home. Sum of the supported lines. Zero when the filer has no deductible expenses. Incomplete when expenses were claimed but no line was selected, or a selected amount is still blank. 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162).

Fact.Name: Schedule C business needs a form this tool does not compute
Fact.Description: True when inventory, a vehicle, depreciation, depletion, equipment rent, a home office, the line 27a deduction, a non-50-percent meal, wage credits, interest that must be allocated, new amortization, a fourth Part V line, or line 6 income that belongs on another form applies. A yes on any stop boolean is enough; later blanks do not turn it off.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 31 is a loss
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sc--dft.pdf), line 32: complete line 32 only when there is a loss. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16: you do not complete line 32 if line 7 is more than the total of lines 28 and 30. A profit is not an at-risk or passive stop.

Fact.Name: All investment is at risk
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 32a. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Line 32. 26 U.S.C. 465 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/465). All at risk, together with material participation, lets the loss flow. Line 32b (some investment is not at risk) needs Form 6198 and stops the return.

Fact.Name: Schedule C loss needs Form 6198 or Form 8582
Fact.Description: A loss without material participation needs Form 8582. 26 U.S.C. 469 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469). A loss that is not fully at risk needs Form 6198. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Lines 31 and 32. A profit does not use this stop. The loss amount itself is still computed; this fact only stops filing, so the limit does not depend on the net in a circle.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 32a
Fact.Description: Checked only for a loss when all investment is at risk.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 32b
Fact.Description: Checked only for a loss when some investment is not at risk. That return is stopped.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business is out of scope
Fact.Description: False when the line-item questions were not started, so a single expense total is not an out-of-scope business. True when they were started and a form stop or a loss-limit stop applies.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses that are out of scope
Fact.Description: Businesses whose line-item answers need a form or a loss limit this tool does not compute.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C line needs a form or loss limit not computed here
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when a Schedule C business, after the line-item questions are started, has inventory (Part III), car or truck expenses or vehicle-loan interest (lines 9 and 16b, Form 4562), depreciation or section 179 (line 13, Form 4562), depletion (line 12), rent of vehicles or equipment (line 20a), business use of the home (line 30, Form 8829 or the simplified method), the energy efficient commercial buildings deduction (line 27a, Form 7205), meals that are not limited to 50 percent (line 24b, 26 U.S.C. 274(n)), wages reduced by an employment credit (line 26), interest that must be allocated (lines 16a and 16c), amortization that begins this year (Form 4562-B), a fourth Part V line, line 6 income that belongs on Form 4136, 6478, or 4797, a loss without material participation (Form 8582, 26 U.S.C. 469), or a loss that is not fully at risk (line 32b, Form 6198, 26 U.S.C. 465). Complete and false when self-employment income was not asked, was answered no, there are no businesses, or the business only has the single expense total. An unanswered line-item question on a business that was started stays incomplete, so that return is not treated as in scope.

Fact.Name: Total Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Sum of Schedule C net profit/(loss) for Schedule 1 line 3 → Form 1040 line 8 (via Schedule 1 line 10). Cite: Schedule C instructions; Form 1040 Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit included in earned income
Fact.Description: Earned income from self-employment for the EITC, CDCC and ACTC = Schedule C net profit (Schedule SE line 3) minus the deductible part of SE tax (Schedule 1 line 15, Schedule SE line 13), 26 U.S.C. 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32#c_2_A): "net earnings from self-employment ... determined with regard to the deduction allowed to the taxpayer by section 164(f)". Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, Part 1: "1a. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 3. ... d. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 13. ... e. Subtract line 1d from line 1c." Under $400 of net earnings no SE tax applies, so this is the Schedule C line 31 net profit (Worksheet B Part 2, line 2b). 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5, lines 4 and 5: "2. The amount shown on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 3, minus any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15." #117: floored at $0 because a loss is not modeled; a loss stops the return wherever it would change a credit (/flowKnockoutScheduleCEarnedIncomeCredits).
